To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the TID-induced degradation of the transconductance and transconductance frequency (fT) of FB and TB SOI NMOS is similar and the degradation of TDBC SOI NMOS devices is significantly less.
The RF degradation of the FB devices is significantly higher than the TB and TDBC devices, which are comparable.
TDBC devices show a significant improvement in RF performance compared to the other structures.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the RF response of 130 nm NMOS transistores.
the radiation-induced degradation of the RF performance of SOI MOSFETs and its impact on the circuit performance.

the radiation-induced RF performance degradation in the input-output and core transistions of a 130 nm SOICMOS technology, and with the impact of body contact at the PDSOI on radiation-induced RF behavior.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the TID-induced performance degradation of the FB and TB transistors is comparable.
the use of a TDBC structure is beneficial to the RF performance, while the FB structure has a better radiation tolerance.
the TDBC structure has the best RF TID performance among the structures investigated.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the TID-induced performance degradation of the SOI devices is dominated by the body effect.
the FB SOI devices are more susceptible to radiation-induced performance degradation than TB and TDBC SOI devices.
the FB structure is not recommended for RF applications.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of body contacts in SOI devices can be used to mitigate TID-induced RF degradation.
, the use of a body contact at the PDSOI is a viable solution for mitigating the radiation-induced performance degradation of the input/output transistors.
the TDBC structure is the most robust against TID irradiation.
